B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires a Pipedrive account and OAuth authorization. Claude setup requires permission to install and use connectors; ChatGPT setup instructions require Developer mode. B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Pipedrive controls plan entitlements and OAuth scopes; Pipedrive user permissions govern records; the customer organization and AI-client administrators control connector availability and installation.

The endpoint publishes OAuth protected-resource metadata naming https://oauth.pipedrive.com as authorization server. Its metadata lists authorization-code and refresh-token grants, PKCE methods S256 and plain, dynamic registration endpoint, client_secret_basic and client_secret_post token authentication, and supported scopes: activities:full, admin, base, contact-fields:full, contacts:full, deal-fields:full, deals:full, leads:full, mail-sending:full, mail:full, product-fields:full, products:full, project-fields:full, projects:full, search:read, users:read. Authorization-server metadata says resource indicators are unsupported and PAR is not required. Token lifetime is not provided; revocation endpoint is https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/revoke. Endpoint POST evidence returned HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC Invalid Request; the separately supplied connection-test evidence reports HTTP 401.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. The official tool reference names read and write operations; it shows no delete tool. No readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations are published.
2. The docs describe OAuth user consent, but no MCP-enforced per-action confirmation flow, preview step, or elicitation mechanism. Pipedrive recommends reviewing each change before approval; this is client/user guidance.
3. OAuth metadata publishes the scopes listed in C. Pipedrive says access follows the user's existing role and visibility permissions. Claude setup requires connector-install permissions. Token lifetime, org-level admin switch defaults, client allowlists, redirect-URI approval rules, and token revocation behavior beyond the published revocation endpoint are undocumented.
4. The input is one global endpoint. No read-only mode, toolset filter, query-free mode, sandbox endpoint, or region-specific endpoint was found. Claude may not load every tool by default; its connector configuration can load all available tools. Email tools require connected email sync; Projects tools require the Projects add-on.
5. The vendor says the assistant can access only data the user is permitted to view or edit. No field masking, PII exclusion, or additional MCP-specific data boundary was found.
6. The vendor states plan token limits apply and additional tokens can be purchased. Exact quota amounts, rate limits, bulk caps, result truncation, and per-call prices are undocumented.
7. Input schemas, validation rules, coercion, unknown-argument behavior, and server-side parameter overrides are undocumented; no public MCP code was available to inspect.
8. Pipedrive states actions are recorded in its change logs. MCP-specific telemetry contents, opt-out, and retention are undocumented.
9. No feedback, rating, survey, report, upsell, or marketing tool appears in the official 51-name tool list. No such instruction or result behavior was documented.
10. No MCP-delivered skills or server instructions were found. Documentation provides client-side setup guidance; it is not documented as server-enforced behavior.
11. No documented behavior indicates that past agent activity changes future outputs, tools, resources, or prompts.
12. The input is documented as Pipedrive's hosted native server. No hierarchy, sub-server proxy, or dynamically loaded server-side toolset was documented.
13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or universal request tool appears in the official tool list.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public source code or verbatim complete tool schemas and initialize instructions were available. The official tool reference provides names and short summaries only.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The official MCP list contains no delete tools, while Pipedrive's product supports record management through its user interface and API; the reviewed MCP documentation does not claim deletion support. Sources: https://support.pipedrive.com/en/article/mcp-tools ; https://developers.pipedrive.com/docs/api/v1

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Pipedrive tells users to refresh the tool list when new tools are added and notes that Claude may not load all tools by default. It advises reviewing changes before approval; the docs do not say the server enforces review. Exact quotes: “As new tools are added to Pipedrive MCP, you may need to refresh the tools list to access the latest available tools.” and “Review the requested permissions in the Pipedrive pop-up and click ”Allow and install” to complete the installation process.”
F_documentation.governance_promises: Pipedrive says access follows existing Pipedrive permissions and that actions are recorded in change logs. Its page says: “Your AI assistant can only access and modify data your Pipedrive user already has permission to view and edit. All actions are recorded in the change log for full auditability.”
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Pipedrive describes the connection as built and maintained by Pipedrive, using real-time CRM data and OAuth; it says access is limited to data within the user's permissions. The AI provider's own privacy and security policies also apply.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance is stated in vendor docs. Change-log recording is a vendor promise, with no implementation detail or independent MCP-specific audit evidence in the reviewed sources. User review and tool-refresh guidance are text-only. No published public code was available to verify server-side enforcement.

The supplied endpoint POST evidence says HTTP 400 with a JSON-RPC invalid-request body; the input's connection-test evidence reports HTTP 401 for an OAuth-protected JSON-RPC endpoint. These are distinct probes and indicate different response conditions.
observations_for_research: The OAuth metadata advertises broad write-capable scopes, including admin and mail-sending:full; actual access is also described as bounded by the user's existing Pipedrive role and visibility permissions.
The official reference and third-party listings differ in breadth and naming, and the official page says clients may not load all tools by default.
The documented tool list includes email and project tools with separate product prerequisites: connected email sync and the Projects add-on.
notes: Checked links.json, pages/INDEX.txt, links_check.txt, official tool-reference pages and scripts, endpoint origin and path captures, OAuth evidence supplied in the prompt, vendor feature and newsroom pages, legal pages, and catalogue copies.
